title: BRIDGE: Triangular Fixed-Point Refinement for Long-Horizon Persona Consistency
claim: A frozen backbone's hidden states pass through coupled refinement and memory-update modules that yield a control signal conditioning the decoder.
layout: Top row flow, three module panels below, control path to bottom row
description: A block diagram that reads left to right across the top, then downward. The top row runs Input Text to a Shared LLM Backbone to Hidden States, joined by arrows. Hidden states then split into three boxed panels. The left panel, Dual-System Processing, shows a fast (green) and a slow (blue) attention system with small matrix icons, plus a red Axial Fusion block. The centre panel, Triangular Fixed-Point Refinement, shows a triangle with nodes for Observable (blue), Latent (purple) and Memory (orange), joined by curved arrows. The right panel, Memory Evolution, stacks Memory State (t-1), a Memory Update Process with three numbered steps, and Memory State (t), using episodic (yellow), affective (red) and personality (purple) colors. Dashed purple and orange lines connect the panels. The triangle's output (o*, l*, m*) becomes a Control Signal. A bottom row runs through Spiral Gating, conditioned hidden states and LLM Decoding to Output Response. The eye goes first to the blue and green headers and the central triangle.
caption: Overview of BRIDGE. The key insight is that Observable (O), Latent (L), and Memory (M) must be jointly refined before
abstract: Long-horizon dialogue agents suffer from latent state drift: what an agent says, what it internally represents, and what it stores in memory can diverge silently across turns. This creates asymmetric rupture risk—many locally coherent exchanges undone by a single high-cost contradiction. We propose BRIDGE (Behavioral Reasoning through Integrated Dynamic Gated Evolution), which performs triangular fixed-point refinement to explicitly couple Observable ($\mathcal{O}$), Latent ($\mathcal{L}$), and Memory ($\mathcal{M}$) before decoding each response. We prove that under mild conditions, the refinement operator converges to a unique fixed point, providing a theoretical guarantee that the agent's internal state remains self-consistent before each response. Empirically, BRIDGE achieves the highest scores on both PersonaGym (4.59 avg., surpassing Claude-3.7-Sonnet) and CoSER (59.5% avg., +3.1 over Claude-3.7-Sonnet), with gains concentrated on persona-specific metrics (+8.0 Character Fidelity over Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct)—while updating only 0.85% trainable parameters of the frozen backbone. We also provide a Lyapunov-style uniform drift bound for tiered memory updates, grounding bounded persona evolution in long-horizon interaction.
